_comment: Your own trust decisions and extra indicators. Copied into this plugin's private folder the
first time it runs; edit the copy, not this one. The path is shown at the bottom of the
trusted  - SHA-256 content hashes you have decided are fine. A match sets the verdict to
Trusted, unless something critical is found anyway. Get the hash from the report.
denied   - SHA-256 hashes, or plugin ids, you consider malicious. A match is reported as
Known bad. Useful for sharing a list with people you trust.
patterns - extra regular expressions, matched case-insensitively against every readable file
in a package and reported as high severity. Add an endpoint or string from an
advisory here rather than waiting for a new build of the scanner.
version / updated / source - what this list is, when it was made and where it came from.
The scanner shows these, and how many days old the file is, on its About section.
Ships blank because this copy is yours and starts empty. Fill them in when you
import or curate a list, so a report can be read against known definitions.
This file deliberately ships with no hashes. A list of allegedly malicious plugin hashes
invented by the scanner's author would be worthless, and one fetched from a server would put a
network dependency in the middle of a security decision. Populate it from sources you trust,
or fold one in with the scanner's "import PATH" command.
